back: A company that operates in more than one country; also called a multinational.
A country in which a TNC sets up a factory, mine, office or shop.
Investment by a company from one country in factories, mines or businesses in another.
Profits from a TNC's operations being sent back to its home country instead of staying in the host country.
Headquarters and research in HICs; regional offices; production (owned or subcontracted) in MICs and LICs; sales worldwide.

front: Why TNCs locate in LICs and MICs
back: Cheap labour, raw materials, growing markets, avoiding tariffs, government incentives, weaker regulations.
